definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Bosh sohasi. The uppermost part of the body containing the brain, eyes, ears, nose, and mouth. The skull (cranium) protects the brain, while the face contains the primary sensory organs.
description_en: The uppermost part of the body containing the brain, eyes, ears, nose, and mouth. The skull (cranium) protects the brain, while the face contains the primary sensory organs.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Yuz sohasi. The anterior part of the head from the forehead to the chin. Contains muscles of facial expression, the orbits housing the eyes, the nasal cavity, oral cavity, and associated structures.
description_en: The anterior part of the head from the forehead to the chin. Contains muscles of facial expression, the orbits housing the eyes, the nasal cavity, oral cavity, and associated structures.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Bo'yin sohasi. The region connecting the head to the trunk. Contains the cervical vertebrae, major blood vessels (carotid arteries, jugular veins), the larynx, pharynx, trachea, esophagus, thyroid gland, and numerous muscles and nerves.
description_en: The region connecting the head to the trunk. Contains the cervical vertebrae, major blood vessels (carotid arteries, jugular veins), the larynx, pharynx, trachea, esophagus, thyroid gland, and numerous muscles and nerves.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Ko'krak qafasi sohasi. The chest region bounded by the rib cage. Contains the lungs, heart, great vessels, esophagus, trachea, and thoracic duct. The thoracic cage provides protection for vital organs while allowing respiratory movements.
description_en: The chest region bounded by the rib cage. Contains the lungs, heart, great vessels, esophagus, trachea, and thoracic duct. The thoracic cage provides protection for vital organs while allowing respiratory movements.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Qorin sohasi. The region between the thorax and pelvis containing the majority of digestive organs including the stomach, intestines, liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, and kidneys. The abdominal wall consists of layered muscles providing support and movement.
description_en: The region between the thorax and pelvis containing the majority of digestive organs including the stomach, intestines, liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, and kidneys. The abdominal wall consists of layered muscles providing support and movement.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Chanoq sohasi. The lower trunk region formed by the pelvic girdle. Contains the urinary bladder, rectum, and reproductive organs. The bony pelvis supports the weight of the upper body and provides attachment for lower limb muscles.
description_en: The lower trunk region formed by the pelvic girdle. Contains the urinary bladder, rectum, and reproductive organs. The bony pelvis supports the weight of the upper body and provides attachment for lower limb muscles.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Orqa / Bel sohasi. The posterior aspect of the trunk from the neck to the pelvis. Contains the vertebral column (spine), spinal cord, and layers of muscles responsible for posture, trunk movement, and protection of the spinal cord.
description_en: The posterior aspect of the trunk from the neck to the pelvis. Contains the vertebral column (spine), spinal cord, and layers of muscles responsible for posture, trunk movement, and protection of the spinal cord.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Yelka sohasi. The region between the shoulder and elbow containing the humerus bone. Major muscles include the biceps brachii (flexion) and triceps brachii (extension). The brachial artery and major nerves traverse this region.
description_en: The region between the shoulder and elbow containing the humerus bone. Major muscles include the biceps brachii (flexion) and triceps brachii (extension). The brachial artery and major nerves traverse this region.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Bilak sohasi. The region between the elbow and wrist containing the radius and ulna bones. Houses the flexor and extensor muscle groups that control hand and wrist movements, as well as the radial and ulnar arteries.
description_en: The region between the elbow and wrist containing the radius and ulna bones. Houses the flexor and extensor muscle groups that control hand and wrist movements, as well as the radial and ulnar arteries.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Qo'l panjasi sohasi. The terminal part of the upper limb consisting of the carpals (wrist bones), metacarpals, and phalanges (finger bones). Contains intrinsic muscles, tendons, and an extensive nerve supply enabling fine motor control and tactile sensation.
description_en: The terminal part of the upper limb consisting of the carpals (wrist bones), metacarpals, and phalanges (finger bones). Contains intrinsic muscles, tendons, and an extensive nerve supply enabling fine motor control and tactile sensation.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Son sohasi. The region between the hip and knee containing the femur, the longest and strongest bone in the body. Major muscle groups include the quadriceps (extension), hamstrings (flexion), and adductors. The femoral artery provides major blood supply.
description_en: The region between the hip and knee containing the femur, the longest and strongest bone in the body. Major muscle groups include the quadriceps (extension), hamstrings (flexion), and adductors. The femoral artery provides major blood supply.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Boldir sohasi. The region between the knee and ankle containing the tibia and fibula bones. The anterior and posterior compartments house muscles controlling ankle dorsiflexion and plantarflexion, as well as the anterior and posterior tibial arteries.
description_en: The region between the knee and ankle containing the tibia and fibula bones. The anterior and posterior compartments house muscles controlling ankle dorsiflexion and plantarflexion, as well as the anterior and posterior tibial arteries.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Oyoq panjasi sohasi. The terminal part of the lower limb consisting of the tarsals, metatarsals, and phalanges. The foot contains arches (medial longitudinal, lateral longitudinal, transverse) that distribute body weight and absorb shock during locomotion.
description_en: The terminal part of the lower limb consisting of the tarsals, metatarsals, and phalanges. The foot contains arches (medial longitudinal, lateral longitudinal, transverse) that distribute body weight and absorb shock during locomotion.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Yelka bo'g'imi sohasi. The junction between the upper limb and trunk. The shoulder girdle consists of the clavicle and scapula, with the glenohumeral joint being the most mobile joint in the body. The rotator cuff muscles stabilize the joint.
description_en: The junction between the upper limb and trunk. The shoulder girdle consists of the clavicle and scapula, with the glenohumeral joint being the most mobile joint in the body. The rotator cuff muscles stabilize the joint.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Chanoq-son sohasi. The junction between the lower limb and trunk. The hip joint (coxal joint) is a ball-and-socket joint formed by the femoral head and acetabulum of the pelvis. Surrounded by powerful muscles, it provides stability for weight-bearing and locomotion.
description_en: The junction between the lower limb and trunk. The hip joint (coxal joint) is a ball-and-socket joint formed by the femoral head and acetabulum of the pelvis. Surrounded by powerful muscles, it provides stability for weight-bearing and locomotion.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Umurtqa pog'onasi sohasi. The vertebral column consisting of 33 vertebrae (7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral fused, 4 coccygeal fused). It protects the spinal cord, supports the head and trunk, and allows flexible movement. Intervertebral discs provide cushioning between vertebrae.
description_en: The vertebral column consisting of 33 vertebrae (7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral fused, 4 coccygeal fused). It protects the spinal cord, supports the head and trunk, and allows flexible movement. Intervertebral discs provide cushioning between vertebrae.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Bosh miya sohasi. The primary organ of the central nervous system enclosed within the cranium. Consists of the cerebrum (cerebral cortex and white matter), cerebellum, brainstem, and diencephalon. The brain processes sensory information, controls motor function, and is the seat of consciousness, cognition, and emotion.
description_en: The primary organ of the central nervous system enclosed within the cranium. Consists of the cerebrum (cerebral cortex and white matter), cerebellum, brainstem, and diencephalon. The brain processes sensory information, controls motor function, and is the seat of consciousness, cognition, and emotion.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Yurak sohasi (Mediastinum). The mediastinal region centered on the heart and great vessels. The heart occupies the middle mediastinum and is enclosed in the pericardium. Major structures include the ascending aorta, superior vena cava, pulmonary trunk, and pulmonary veins.
description_en: The mediastinal region centered on the heart and great vessels. The heart occupies the middle mediastinum and is enclosed in the pericardium. Major structures include the ascending aorta, superior vena cava, pulmonary trunk, and pulmonary veins.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Ko'z sohasi (Orbita). The orbital region containing the eyeball and its accessory structures. The eye converts light into neural signals for visual perception. Structures include the cornea, lens, retina, iris, and optic nerve, along with extraocular muscles, eyelids, and the lacrimal apparatus.
description_en: The orbital region containing the eyeball and its accessory structures. The eye converts light into neural signals for visual perception. Structures include the cornea, lens, retina, iris, and optic nerve, along with extraocular muscles, eyelids, and the lacrimal apparatus.

definition_uz: Inson tanasi sohasi: Quloq sohasi. The region containing the external, middle, and inner ear structures. The ear converts sound waves into neural signals for auditory perception and contains the vestibular apparatus for balance. Key structures include the tympanic membrane, ossicles, cochlea, and semicircular canals.
description_en: The region containing the external, middle, and inner ear structures. The ear converts sound waves into neural signals for auditory perception and contains the vestibular apparatus for balance. Key structures include the tympanic membrane, ossicles, cochlea, and semicircular canals.
